Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.

spec.name: Box Bot Kid
spec.description: A kid in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume: kraft-brown box torso and box head with a face window, drawn-on control panel, tube gauntlets, mitten hands, sneakers and a rocket pack with tissue-paper flames.
spec.layout: A kid about 1.5 m tall stands on the floor at x=0 facing +Z, wearing a cardboard robot costume. A big kraft-brown box torso (0.64 wide in x, 0.46 deep in z, y 0.55 to 1.02) sits over the kid's hips; a smaller box head (0.46 wide, 0.38 deep, y 1.02 to 1.40) stacks on top of it, with a rectangular window cut in the head's front wall (center [0, 1.21, 0.19], 0.22 wide, 0.19 tall) through which the kid's round head, hair, eyes and smile peek out. The kid's arms stick out of taped arm holes in the torso sides: blue T-shirt sleeves, skin forearms, cardboard-tube gauntlets with drawn stripes and tape rings, and chunky mitten hands hanging at y ~0.45-0.50. The kid's legs show below the box hem: denim shorts, skin shins, white socks and red sneakers with white soles resting on y=0. The torso front wears a marker-drawn control panel with foil dials and coloured buttons, a hand-painted red lightning-bolt emblem above it, and a horizontal tape band at the hem; packing tape strips run down the box corners and across the head box. A foil ear disc sits on each side of the head box, and an antenna with a foil ball rises to y ~1.58 on the head top. On the back, a cardboard rocket pack with two angled thruster tubes and tissue-paper flame cones (orange outside, yellow core) sticks off the torso. Style is cardboard craft throughout: flat kraft-brown cardboard, grey-beige packing tape, dark marker lines, hand-painted red/green/amber accents, silver foil, chunky low-poly shapes with slightly hand-made wobble.

parts.builds: The costume's main cardboard box body: a hollow five-sided kraft box (outer x -0.32..0.32, y 0.55..1.02, z -0.23..0.23, wall thickness ~0.012, open bottom for the legs and open top under the head box, so inner walls show kraftDark). Front wall carries, seated proud of the surface: a marker-outlined control panel (kraftLight paper rectangle ~0.34 x 0.18 centered [0, 0.72, 0.232] with a dark marker border) holding two foil dials (r 0.032 at x +/-0.09 with marker pointer lines), a red, a green and an amber button (r 0.015, row at y 0.75), a small slider slot, and a drawn gauge with a needle; above it a hand-painted red lightning-bolt emblem (~0.14 tall, centered [0, 0.90, 0.232]) with a marker outline. Tape strips (tape colour, thin flat quads) run vertically down all four box corners, a horizontal tape band rings the box at y 0.575 as hem reinforcement, and a second short tape strip crosses the front lower edge. Left and right walls each have a round arm hole (r 0.075) centered on the shoulderL/shoulderR mounts with a taped rim ring around each hole. Back wall left plain except two tape patches where the jetpack mounts sit (packBack). A couple of marker-drawn seam lines trace the top and bottom edges. Everything slightly wobbly and hand-made; no joints of its own beyond riding body.
parts.attaches: Top face open under the head box at mount boxTop; arm holes ring the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts; bottom hem (y 0.55) sits over the legs part's shorts at hipL/hipR; back wall meets the jetpack at packBack.

parts.builds: The robot head shell: a smaller kraft cardboard box (outer x -0.23..0.23, y 1.02..1.40, z -0.19..0.19, walls ~0.012, hollow, open bottom resting on the torso top, inner faces kraftDark). Its front wall has a rectangular window cut fully through (opening 0.22 wide, 0.19 tall, centered [0, 1.21, 0.19]) framed by a taped edge strip all round the cut. Tape strips run along the top edges and down the front corners; three marker-drawn rivet dots sit on the front wall below the window (y 1.08). A foil ear disc (r 0.045, ~0.015 thick) sticks out of each side wall at [ +/-0.235, 1.21, 0.02 ]. On top at [0.09, 1.40, 0.02] an antenna: a small kraftDark base disc, a thin kraft rod (r 0.008, ~0.16 tall) and a foil ball (r 0.03) on top reaching y ~1.59. Maybe one small bent cardboard flap (kraftLight) peeling off the top rear corner for the hand-made feel.
parts.attaches: Sits on the torso box top at mount boxTop (bottom rim at y 1.02); the kidFace part builds into the window at mount faceWindow.

parts.builds: The kid's head peeking through the costume's face window: a round skin head (r ~0.135, centered [0, 1.20, 0.06], the face front just proud of the window plane at z ~0.2), with ears (small skin discs, r 0.028) on both sides, and chunky brown hair as a hair-cap of a few overlapping rounded blobs on top and back of the skull in hair colour, plus a couple of loose fringe tufts over the forehead. The face is the hero: two big eyes (eyeWhite ellipses ~0.035 wide with iris pupils and tiny white catchlights), drawn-on eyebrow strokes (marker) above them, a small skin nose bump, a wide happy open smile (dark mouth shape with a tiny white tooth glint) low on the face, and two round rosy cheek dots. A short skin neck cylinder runs down from the head into the box, with the collar of the kid's blue T-shirt visible as a blue ring around the neck base. The whole head is visible only through the window, so keep features centred on the window opening.
parts.attaches: Head sits inside the headBox, face emerging from the window at mount faceWindow; neck rides the head joint.

parts.builds: Both of the kid's arms, hanging in a relaxed pose with a slight forward lean: at each shoulder mount (shoulderL/shoulderR) a blue T-shirt sleeve stub (short tube r 0.06, ~0.06 long) with a taped rim where it meets the box arm hole; then a skin upper-arm tube (r 0.045) down to the elbow at [ +/-0.40, 0.75, 0.06 ]; then a cardboard tube gauntlet (kraft, r 0.055, from elbow to wrist at [ +/-0.43, 0.56, 0.08 ]) decorated with two tape rings, a marker-drawn stripe down its outer face and one small drawn dial (foil circle r 0.018 with a marker pointer); then a chunky mitten hand (kraft, rounded box ~0.09 x 0.11 x 0.06 with a thumb stub on the inner side, and a marker-drawn cuff line at the wrist). Hands hang at y ~0.45-0.50, palms facing inward. Both arms are mirrored builds of the same recipe.
parts.attaches: Sleeves plug into the torso box arm holes at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR; each arm rides its armL/handL or armR/handR joints.

parts.builds: Both of the kid's legs below the box hem, standing straight with feet flat on the floor: at each hip mount (hipL/hipR) a denim shorts stub (tube r 0.075, y 0.50..0.56, the top tucked just under the torso box hem) with a drawn cuff line; then a skin shin (r 0.05) down to the ankle at [ +/-0.13, 0.12, 0.02 ]; a white sock ring (sock, y 0.10..0.155, slightly wider than the shin, with a small fold bump at the top); and a red sneaker per foot: a rounded shoe body (shoe, ~0.10 wide x 0.09 tall, from y 0 to 0.09, extending z -0.05..0.14 so the toe points forward), a white sole slab (sole, ~0.03 thick, y 0..0.03, slightly wider than the shoe, a white toe cap, three small lace dots on the tongue and a short side stripe in sole colour. Soles rest exactly on y=0. Both legs are mirrored builds of the same recipe.
parts.attaches: Shorts tops tuck under the torso box hem at mounts hipL and hipR; each leg rides its legL/footL or legR/footR joints; soles on the floor.

parts.builds: A homemade cardboard rocket pack stuck to the back of the torso box: two thruster units mounted at [ +/-0.14, 0.82, -0.24 ] on the packBack mount, each a kraft cardboard tube (r 0.06, ~0.16 long) angled outward and down (axis about [ +/-0.15, -0.35, -0.92 ]), each with a foil rim ring at its rear opening, a red painted band around its middle, and a small marker-drawn dot row down its side; from each rear opening a tissue-paper flame sticks out (a soft flame cone ~0.13 long in flame orange with a smaller flameCore yellow cone inside, slightly wavy tips). The two thrusters are tied together by a short tape strip across the pack at y 0.86, and each tube wears a tape patch where it meets the box back. No propellant hardware beyond the drawn details - keep it simple and toy-like.
parts.attaches: Tape patches and tube roots seat on the torso box back wall at mount packBack; rides the body joint.

calls.reasoning:
The user wants me to create a shared specification (JSON) for a model of a kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
This model will be built by multiple agents using the `agentic-3js-builder` SDK, following a detailed set of instructions.

**Model Analysis:**
- **Subject:** Kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
- **Style:** Cardboard craft, stylized, low-poly, bold shapes, readable proportions.
-I need to write a shared spec for a kid in a cardboard-box robot costume, cardboard craft style. Not module code — just the JSON spec.

Let me think about the model: a kid wearing a cardboard box as a robot body/head. Classic: a big cardboard box torso with a smaller box head on top (or the box covers head+torso with a cutout face), arms made of cardboard tubes/boxes, legs in cardboard boots, drawn-on robot face, dials, knobs, cardboard "jetpack" made of toilet rolls, foil-covered parts, crayon-drawn gauges, etc.

Actually the classic kid-in-a-box costume: the box is the body, head sticks out through a hole at top, or the box covers the head with a face window cut out showing the kid's face. Let me decide: a larger box as torso/head shell with a cut-open "window" on front showing the kid's face peeking out, arms in cardboard sleeves, legs visible in shorts/boots below. That reads well.

Design:
- Kid ~1.2m tall. Cardboard box torso: roughly 0.55 × 0.55 × 0.4 m box from y=0.45 to y=1.0, with a smaller "head box" on top? Or the box torso extends up as the robot head at y=1.0–1.35.

Let me structure:
- Kid's legs (from y=0 to y~0.5): shorts, legs, sneakers.
- Kid's arms emerging from box arm holes: cardboard tube gauntlets, kid hands.
- Kid's head/face peeking out from front window of the box head, with a helmet-ish edge (tinfoil? no, cardboard). Face: skin, hair, big eyes, smile — crayon style.
- Cardboard box body: kraft brown #b98a4f-ish, with tape strips, flaps, drawn-on control panel (dials, buttons), a painted emblem, marker-drawn seams.
- Robot details: drawn-on face on the box? The classic: the box front has a drawn robot face and the kid's real face peeks from a hole. Or kid's face is the robot's face. Let me have: big box covering torso+head (one box from y~0.45 to y~1.45), with a rectangular window cut in front upper area where the kid's face peeks out. Below the window on the box front: drawn control panel with dials/knobs. Arms stick out of side holes with cardboard tube arms and mitten hands. Legs below.

Alternatively kid wears box as torso, and separate smaller box as helmet on head with antenna. Hmm. The "head through hole" version is more iconic for "kid in cardboard box robot costume."

Structure the spec into 4–5 parts:

1. **cardboardBody** — the big box (robot body shell): box walls with tape, flaps, side arm holes, front control panel (dials, knobs, buttons), painted emblem/number, drawn seams, bottom edge skirt. Joints: spine root.
2. **robotHead / headShell** — actually if the box is one big unit covering torso+head, the head hole is in the body part. But spec says parts split work evenly; better to split: lower box (torso, y 0.5–1.0) and upper box (head, y 1.0–1.45) with the face window. Both cardboard.
3. **kidFace** — the kid's head peeking out: head, hair, eyes, ears, cheeks, maybe a beanie? Face inside the window frame. Own joints: head, jaw maybe.
4. **arms** — cardboard tube gauntlets with mitten hands, kid arms, drawn stripes on tubes. Joints: armL, armR (hinge).
5. **legs** — shorts, legs, sneakers, socks. Joints: legL, legR (leg).
6. **backpack / jetpack** — cardboard rockets on the back (toilet-roll tubes as thrusters), tissue paper flames? Cardboard jet pack with two tube thrusters and paper "flames" — fun detail. Could fold into body part.

Budget total ≤900; aim ~800: body 220, head 150, face 160, arms 130, legs 120, jetpack 80 → 860. That's 6 parts, allowed 3–6. Good.

Mounts:
- bodyTop: where head box sits on torso box: [0, 1.0, 0] (top face of torso, center).
- faceHole / windowCenter: front face of head box: [0, 1.22, 0.21]? Need the head box front z. Let me define dimensions.

Model size: width ~1.1 (arms out slightly or at sides), height ~1.5 (antenna adds to ~1.6), depth ~0.6. Let's set size [1.2, 1.65, 0.65].

Kid standing centered x=0, facing +Z.

Torso box: from y=0.55 to y=1.02, width 0.62 (x -0.31..0.31), depth 0.44 (z -0.22..0.22). Actually kid should stand inside; legs below box at y 0–0.6ish. Box bottom edge at y=0.55 — box hem. Legs: y 0 to 0.55 visible below box (shorts hidden mostly? Actually box covers hips; legs show from under box: thighs partially, then shins, sneakers).

Hmm, typical: box worn like a costume body, bottom open, kid's legs show below box hem at y≈0.5. Legs go 0→0.55.

Head box: from y=1.02 to y=1.42, width 0.46 (x -0.23..0.23), depth 0.38 (z -0.19..0.19). Face window on front: rectangular cutout, center z=0.19, y≈1.2, size 0.24 wide × 0.2 high. Kid's head (sphere ~0.13 radius) peeks through, face at z≈0.2.

Antenna on top: thin stick with ball, at [0.08, 1.42, 0] to ~1.58. Total height 1.6.

Arms: shoulder joints at sides of torso box: [±0.35, 0.95, 0]. Cardboard tube arms hang down: upper arm from shoulder, tube gauntlet forearm, mitten hand. Arms length ~0.45, hands at y≈0.5.

Legs: joints hipL/hipR at [±0.12, 0.55, 0], legs down to feet at y=0. Sneakers at z≈0.05.

Jetpack: two toilet-roll thrusters on back of torso box: at [±0.16, 0.85, -0.26], pointing back-down, with orange/red tissue-paper flame cones.

- body (root): at [0, 0.8, 0], dir [0,1,0], role spine — rides the torso box? The box is rigid; the root joint just holds everything.
- head: parent body, at [0, 1.02, 0], dir [0,1,0], role head — head box.
- jaw? Not needed — kid face static. Could add jaw for smile. Keep static? Requirements: rigged models have root joint; roles. Let me include armL, armR (hinge), legL, legR (leg), handL, handR (digit?). Keep it simple: 
  - body root spine at [0,0.8,0]
  - head parent body at [0,1.02,0] dir [0,1,0] role head
  - armL parent body at [0.36,0.95,0.02] dir [0.15,-1,0.1] role arm (bone points down along arm)

Keep it modest: body, head, armL, armR, legL, legR, plus handL/handR and footL/footR optional. I'll include hands and feet for riggability.

Order: body, head, armL, handL, armR, handR, legL, footL, legR, footR. Parents first.

Wait — hand parent armL must come after armL. Fine.

Mounts:
- boxTop: [0, 1.02, 0] — head box sits on torso box.
- window: [0, 1.2, 0.19] — face window center on head box front face; kidFace builds into it.
- shoulderL: [0.36, 0.95, 0.02], shoulderR: [-0.36, 0.95, 0.02] — arm holes in torso box sides.
